The y start is snapped DOWN to a page boundary; vertical granularity is 8 rows,

as strongly indicated from the controller's

svg.text: buffer cleared to 0xFF at init; inverse

svg.text: measured: 220,459 µs / full refresh ≈ 91 µs / transaction —
Bring-up sequence — power-on to first refresh
21-entry init table, replayed byte-for-byte, in order

g.text: CMD 0xF1 + DATA 0x4F — set COM end = 79 (80 rows)
leaves an init'd, fed panel dark —

svg.text: Note on step B — why the scroll line matters

g.text: Neither firmware ever programs the controller's row-granular vertical origin, so both inherit whatever the register holds out
of its own power-on reset. On the observed unit that value was 15, and the whole image displayed 15 rows too high — not a
multiple of 8, therefore not a page or window error. (strongly indicated)
Controller family is UC1611/UC1611s-class (strongly indicated) — every opcode used lands in that command map, but three bytes
(0xC9, 0x95 and the 0xE1 preamble) have no row in the public revision of that command table, so they are replayed verbatim
rather than paraphrased. Panel technology, physical size and dot pitch as seen rather than inferred remain unverified.
